messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The issue occurs in the `Base64InputStream.read(byte[])` method, which internally delegates to `Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`. The latter method uses `base64.readResults(byte[], int, int)` to read decoded data. Inspecting `Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`, it has a loop to avoid returning 0 to conform with `InputStreamReader` expectations, but finally relies on `base64.readResults`.

In `Base64.readResults`, if there is no buffer, it checks the `eof` flag and returns -1 if `eof` is true, else returns 0. Returning 0 means no data is currently available but not EOF.

The reported bug is that when `Base64InputStream.read(byte[])` reaches the end of any stream that is a multiple of 3 bytes long, it incorrectly returns 0 instead of -1, causing problems in `InputStreamReader` which expects -1 at EOF. This suggests that `Base64.readResults` returns 0 despite the stream being at end (expected to return -1).

The root cause likely lies in the `eof` flag handling in the `Base64` class, showing that the flag isn't set correctly when the underlying stream ends on multiples of 3 in length. This leads `Base64.readResults` to return 0, incorrectly signaling "no data now" rather than EOF, causing the observed issue.

The comments in `Base64InputStream.read` indicate a loop to handle zero reads from `readResults`, but this only helps when zeroes are due to non-base64 characters. It does not fix end-of-stream zero returns incorrectly made by `readResults`.

Hence, the faulty behavior is in `Base64.readResults` or the underlying logic that sets EOF when decoding streams that are a multiple of 3 bytes long.

The recent bug report about NullPointerException with modulus 3 from a previous entry also suggests some edge case in base64 decoding modulus logic related to stream length not well handled, reinforcing the hypothesis that the handling of EOF and buffer state for streams multiple of 3 bytes is the problem.

This analysis matches the observed symptoms: `Base64InputStream#read(byte[])` incorrectly returning 0 at end of stream for multiples of 3 bytes.

Recommended place to fix is within the `Base64.readResults` method or related decoding logic to correctly detect EOF and not return 0 incorrectly at the end of streams that are multiples of 3 bytes long.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
